subject: How to Work with Islands in inla Mesh.

messages.author: 32c683df57265f82
messages.subject: How to Work with Islands in inla Mesh.
parts:
How does inla mesh interpret non-contiguous polygons, for example islands off-coast of a country?
I have trouble working with country boundaries that also include islands.
Was inla just created to work in all connected/continuous borders enclosing a region?

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] How to Work with Islands in inla Mesh.
parts:
You can build a "mesh with holes and physical boundaries" as you can see

available at http://www.r-inla.org/examples/tutorials

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] How to Work with Islands in inla Mesh.
parts:
On Wed, 2015-06-24 at 06:12 -0700, olweny wrote:
> How does inla mesh interpret non-contiguous polygons, for example
> islands off-coast of a country?

Non-connected parts of a mesh will be treated as independent processes
(but with the same parameters).

> I have trouble working with country boundaries that also include
> islands.
> Was inla just created to work in all connected/continuous borders
> enclosing a region?

If you want dependence between the islands and the mainland, you must
construct a model that is defined also in a region between the islands
and the mainland, so that there is something in the model connecting
them. Whether the values of the process outside both the islands and
mainland then mean anything physically depends entirely on the
application.

Finn
